userStories.title: Generate sprint stories for transcription focus area
acceptanceCriteria: Read scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json to understand the 'transcription' focus area
Read scripts/ralph/session/prompt.md for project context and architecture notes
Read scripts/ralph/state/queue.json for interview details (story outline, architecture decisions, key files)
Read CLAUDE.md for project conventions and known issues
Analyze the codebase to find 8-12 specific improvements for 'transcription'
Add stories US-66-002 through US-66-012 to scripts/ralph/state/prd.json (MUST use sprint-prefixed IDs)
Each story MUST have 4-6 testable acceptance criteria
Each story MUST have a 'notes' field with: (1) tier classification, (2) exact source file paths, (3) line number ranges if removing/moving code
IMPORTANT: All generated stories MUST have passes set to false - do NOT run tests or evaluate whether they already pass

userStories.notes: Seed story completed. Generated 11 stories (US-66-002 through US-66-012) for the transcription focus area based on codebase analysis. Stories cover: duplicate code consolidation, config extraction, validation, thread safety, test coverage, and architectural improvements. Avoided duplicating work from sprints 38, 59, 60, 62.

userStories.title: Consolidate duplicate timestamp parsing into single canonical function
acceptanceCriteria: src/caption/parsers.py:parse_timestamp is the single canonical timestamp parsing function
src/caption_fetcher.py:_parse_timestamp (line ~5136) delegates to or is replaced by src/caption/parsers.py:parse_timestamp
src/caption/normalizer.py:_parse_timestamp (line ~542) delegates to or is replaced by src/caption/parsers.py:parse_timestamp
All three call sites produce identical results for HH:MM:SS.mmm, HH:MM:SS,mmm, and MM:SS.mmm formats
Existing tests in tests/test_caption_normalizer.py and tests/test_caption_fetcher.py still pass
At least 3 new unit tests verify the consolidated function handles edge cases (negative values, missing hours, overflow milliseconds)
userStories.notes: Consolidated parse_timestamp into src/caption/parsers.py. Both caption_fetcher.py and normalizer.py delegate via import. Added negative value guard. 25 unit tests in test_caption_parsers_timestamp.py covering all formats, edge cases (negative values, missing hours, overflow milliseconds), and delegation verification. All existing tests pass.

userStories.title: Consolidate duplicate timestamp formatting (seconds_to_vtt/srt) into single location
acceptanceCriteria: seconds_to_vtt_timestamp and seconds_to_srt_timestamp exist in exactly ONE location (src/caption/normalizer.py or src/caption/parsers.py)
src/caption_fetcher.py:seconds_to_vtt_timestamp (line ~7537) and seconds_to_srt_timestamp (line ~7557) are removed or delegate to the canonical location
All callers import from the single canonical location
Existing tests in tests/test_caption_normalizer.py still pass
At least 2 new unit tests verify formatting edge cases (0 seconds, very large values > 99 hours)
userStories.notes: Canonical implementations remain in src/caption/normalizer.py. caption_fetcher.py now delegates via _CanonicalNormalizer import. Added 3 new tests: >99h VTT, >99h SRT, delegation verification. All 16 timestamp tests pass.

acceptanceCriteria: CaptionCircuitBreakerConfig is defined in exactly ONE location
src/caption/circuit_breaker.py imports CaptionCircuitBreakerConfig from src/config/sections/download.py (or vice versa, whichever is the config canonical source)
No duplicate field definitions exist between the two files
CaptionCircuitBreaker class still functions correctly with the single config source
tests/test_caption_circuit_breaker.py passes without modification (or with minimal import path updates)
userStories.notes: Removed duplicate 30-line CaptionCircuitBreakerConfig class from src/caption/circuit_breaker.py. Replaced with import from canonical src/config/sections/download.py (Rule 11). Re-exported via noqa comment so all existing imports from src.caption.circuit_breaker continue to work unchanged. 312 tests pass (297 config/circuit-breaker + 15 integration).

userStories.title: Extract hardcoded batch processor thresholds to CaptionFirstConfig
acceptanceCriteria: progress_report_interval is a field on CaptionFirstConfig (or CaptionBatchConfig) in src/config/sections/download.py with default 25
unavailable_threshold is a field on CaptionFirstConfig in src/config/sections/download.py with default 0.8
src/caption/batch_processor.py reads these values from config instead of hardcoding them (lines ~67-76)
config.yaml documents these new fields under download.caption_first with comments
At least 2 tests verify custom config values are respected by batch_processor
userStories.notes: Added progress_report_interval (default 25) and unavailable_threshold (default 0.8) fields to CaptionFirstConfig in src/config/sections/download.py. Added BatchProcessorConfig.from_caption_first_config() classmethod to bridge config from CaptionFirstConfig to BatchProcessorConfig (supports both object and dict access per Rule 6). Documented both fields in config.yaml under download.caption_first. Added 7 tests in TestBatchProcessorConfigFromCaptionFirst class verifying custom values, defaults, overrides, and dict access. 580 tests pass.

userStories.title: Extract hardcoded rate limit backoff parameters to config
acceptanceCriteria: base_backoff_seconds (default 5.0) is configurable via CaptionFirstConfig or a new RateLimitStateConfig
max_backoff_seconds (default 300.0) is configurable via the same config
max_history (default 10) is configurable via the same config
src/caption/timeout.py RateLimitState dataclass reads from config or accepts these as constructor args
config.yaml documents these fields under download.caption_first with comments
At least 2 tests verify non-default values are propagated correctly
userStories.notes: Tier: config extraction. Files: src/caption/timeout.py (lines 70-72, hardcoded in RateLimitState dataclass), src/config/sections/download.py (CaptionFirstConfig, line ~265). These values control exponential backoff behavior for rate-limited caption fetches. Currently only changeable by editing code.

userStories.title: Add __post_init__ validation for CaptionCircuitBreakerConfig
acceptanceCriteria: CaptionCircuitBreakerConfig has a __post_init__ method that validates: pause_seconds > 0, max_pause_seconds >= pause_seconds, threshold >= 1
Invalid values raise ValueError with a descriptive message
At least 3 tests verify validation: (1) pause_seconds <= 0 raises, (2) max_pause_seconds < pause_seconds raises, (3) threshold < 1 raises
Valid configurations (including edge cases like pause_seconds == max_pause_seconds) pass without error
userStories.notes: Tier: validation. Files: src/config/sections/download.py (CaptionCircuitBreakerConfig, line ~136). Currently has NO __post_init__ validation â€” invalid values like negative pause_seconds or threshold=0 would silently cause bugs at runtime. Pattern: follow CaptionRetryBudgetConfig.__post_init__ (line ~231) which already validates its fields.

userStories.title: Add __post_init__ validation for TranscriptionConfig
acceptanceCriteria: TranscriptionConfig.__post_init__ validates: model is one of known Whisper model names (tiny, base, small, medium, large, large-v2, large-v3)
TranscriptionConfig.__post_init__ validates: minimum_gpu_memory_mb >= 100 (prevents misconfiguration)
TranscriptionConfig.__post_init__ validates: compute_type is one of (auto, float16, int8, float32, int8_float16)
TranscriptionConfig.__post_init__ validates: max_workers >= 1 and batch_size >= 1
At least 4 tests verify each validation rule rejects invalid values with ValueError
Valid default config passes validation without error
userStories.notes: Tier: validation. Files: src/config/sections/core.py (TranscriptionConfig, line ~51). Currently the __post_init__ (line ~111) only handles PauseSplitConfig and audio_extraction_workers. No validation for model names, compute_type, or numeric ranges. Invalid model names would fail at Whisper load time with a cryptic error instead of at config load.

userStories.title: Add thread safety to BatchCaptionCheckpoint.update_progress
acceptanceCriteria: BatchCaptionCheckpoint has a threading.RLock (or uses its existing _lock if present)
update_progress() method (src/caption_fetcher.py line ~950) acquires lock before modifying results, counts, remaining_video_ids, and updated_at
mark_aborted() method (line ~972) also acquires lock before modifying shared state
At least 2 tests verify thread safety: concurrent update_progress calls from multiple threads produce correct counts
No deadlocks when calling update_progress from within a locked context
userStories.notes: Tier: bug fix (thread safety). Files: src/caption_fetcher.py (BatchCaptionCheckpoint class, lines ~936-1027). The update_progress method modifies results dict, success_count, error_count, remaining_video_ids, and updated_at without holding a lock. CaptionMetrics (line ~649) correctly uses _lock for all mutations â€” BatchCaptionCheckpoint should follow the same pattern. Note: the batch processor runs workers concurrently, so this is a real race condition.

userStories.title: Add deprecation warning for legacy transcripts/ cache directory
acceptanceCriteria: TranscriptionCache.__init__ logs a WARNING when alt_cache_dir (transcripts/) contains cached files
Warning message includes migration guidance: 'Move files from transcripts/ to transcriptions/ and delete transcripts/'
New _migrate_legacy_cache() method copies entries from transcripts/ to transcriptions/ when both exist
Migration only runs once per session (guard flag prevents repeated migration)
At least 3 tests verify: (1) no warning when only transcriptions/ exists, (2) warning logged when transcripts/ has files, (3) migration copies files correctly
userStories.notes: Tier: maintenance. Files: src/transcription/cache.py (lines 43-47). Currently checks both transcriptions/ and transcripts/ silently with no indication which is primary or that transcripts/ is legacy. Users may have stale cache in the wrong directory without knowing.

userStories.title: Add transcription config focus area to ralph-config.json
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json has a 'transcription' entry in focusAreas array with id, name, category, description
relevantFiles.transcription lists: src/transcription/, src/caption_fetcher.py, src/caption/, src/stages/caption_stage.py, src/config/sections/core.py (TranscriptionConfig)
testPatterns.transcription lists: test_transcription*.py, test_caption*.py, test_caption_fetcher*.py
The focus area is categorized under 'acquisition' or 'processing' category
Queue.json can now reference 'transcription' as a valid focus area (already referenced, this validates it)
userStories.notes: Tier: config. Files: scripts/ralph/config/ralph-config.json. Currently 'transcription' is used as a focus area in queue.json but is NOT defined in ralph-config.json focusAreas array. Only 'caption' exists there. This means Ralph can't look up test patterns or relevant files for the transcription focus area, falling back to defaults.

userStories.title: Add negative cache expiration test coverage for caption fetcher cache
acceptanceCriteria: At least 3 new tests in tests/test_caption_cache.py or tests/test_caption_enhanced_cache.py cover negative cache TTL behavior
Test 1: Verify is_caption_unavailable returns True for entry within TTL window
Test 2: Verify is_caption_unavailable returns False for entry past TTL (expired)
Test 3: Verify re-fetch succeeds after negative cache entry expires (integration with store_unavailable/is_caption_unavailable cycle)
Tests use time mocking (monkeypatch or freezegun) to control TTL expiration without real waiting
All new tests pass with pytest -v
userStories.notes: Tier: testing. Files: tests/test_caption_cache.py, tests/test_caption_enhanced_cache.py, src/caption_fetcher_cache.py. Sprint 60 (US-60-004) added negative caching with TTL but the test coverage for TTL expiration edge cases is incomplete. Specifically: what happens when TTL is 0 (immediate expiry), very large TTL, and the exact boundary second.
